options_evaluated: Virgin ABS plastic with brominated flame retardants
Post-consumer recycled polypropylene (rPP) without halogenated flame retardants
assessments.recommendation: Post-consumer recycled polypropylene (rPP) without halogenated flame retardants
assessments.rationale: Using recycled PP directly addresses the parameter of recycled content (h) and reduces the material footprint (o) by substituting virgin resources with secondary raw materials as highlighted on Page 2. Avoiding halogenated flame retardants ensures compliance with the substances of concern parameter (f), preventing the impairment of the technical properties, usefulness, or value of the recycled material at end-of-life as detailed on Page 35. Furthermore, PP has a lower density than aluminum or ABS, supporting lightweight design (t) through material savings on Page 80.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use Phase (potential reduction in mechanical durability and impact resistance compared to virgin ABS, which could shorten the product's lifetime if subjected to heavy impacts) and Manufacturing (rPP requires precise shrinkage control and tooling adjustments).
espr_parameters: (h) use or content of recycled materials

options_evaluated: Reversible mechanical fasteners (screws and snap-fits) with material coding
assessments.recommendation: Reversible mechanical fasteners (screws and snap-fits) with material coding
assessments.rationale: This option directly aligns with design for recycling (d) and material footprint (o). As outlined on Page 79, ease of non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly, along with material coding standards for identification, are critical product parameters to facilitate recycling, reuse, and repair without requiring specialized tools.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing (increased assembly time and higher part count compared to rapid ultrasonic welding) and Use Phase (potential for mechanical loosening due to operational vibrations, requiring periodic maintenance).

options_evaluated: High-efficiency brushless DC (BLDC) motor with rare-earth magnets
Standard brushed AC motor with copper windings
Synchronous reluctance motor without rare-earth magnets and incorporating remanufactured rotor components
assessments.recommendation: Synchronous reluctance motor without rare-earth magnets and incorporating remanufactured rotor components
assessments.rationale: This choice prioritizes the incorporation of used components (k) and reduces the material footprint (o) by utilizing remanufactured parts as supported by Page 79 and Page 2. Avoiding rare-earth magnets prevents the introduction of critical raw materials that complicate the recycling process (d) and increase the environmental footprint (m) of raw material extraction (Page 35, Page 33).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use Phase (synchronous reluctance motors may have lower energy efficiency or power density compared to BLDC motors with rare-earth magnets, potentially increasing energy consumption during use).

options_evaluated: Active cooling fan with heavy copper heat sinks
Passive cooling with load- and stress-optimised structural air-ducts integrated into the housing
Liquid cooling loop with synthetic thermal fluids
assessments.recommendation: Passive cooling with load- and stress-optimised structural air-ducts integrated into the housing
assessments.rationale: This approach fulfills lightweight design (t) and reduces the material footprint (o). Page 80 highlights that lightweight design is achieved through the integration of functions within the material or into a single product component and the load- and stress-optimisation of structures. Integrating the cooling path directly into the structural housing eliminates the need for heavy copper heat sinks, reducing overall weight and material consumption.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use Phase (passive cooling may limit the maximum continuous power of the vacuum motor or lead to higher operating temperatures, which could accelerate thermal aging of nearby electronics).

options_evaluated: Monolithic integrated design with molded-in components
Modular architecture with standardized, easily separable functional blocks (motor, battery, cord reel)
Modular design using proprietary connectors and specialized tools
assessments.recommendation: Modular architecture with standardized, easily separable functional blocks (motor, battery, cord reel)
assessments.rationale: This option directly implements design for recycling (d) and reduces the material footprint (o). Page 79 states that ease of repair, modularity, and the use of standard components without specialized tools are key to improving product circularity and reducing waste. Standardized modules allow easy non-destructive disassembly for component recovery or repair.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Packaging and Logistics (modular designs often increase the overall volume and weight of the product and its packaging, potentially conflicting with parameter (j) on Page 80).

options_evaluated: Removable and recyclable corded power module
Modular, user-replaceable Lithium-ion battery pack with cobalt-free chemistry and recycled content
assessments.recommendation: Modular, user-replaceable Lithium-ion battery pack with cobalt-free chemistry and recycled content
assessments.rationale: This option addresses the use of recycled materials (h) and minimizes substances of concern (f). Eliminating cobalt avoids hazardous/critical substances that make recycling more complicated or environmentally impactful (Page 35). Incorporating recycled content reduces the material footprint (o) and dependency on primary raw materials (Page 2). Non-destructive removability supports design for recycling (d) as specified on Page 79.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use Phase (cobalt-free chemistries like LFP have lower energy density, which might increase the battery pack's weight and volume (j), or reduce the vacuum cleaner's runtime per charge).
espr_parameters: (h) use or content of recycled materials
